A RULING TRANSFERS ONLY WHEN ITS FALSIFIER DOES NOT FIRE IN THE NEW LANGUAGE (fleet form 16), so rust implements. BOTH classes are published and split by metadata.attributeKind — builtin_directive (derive, allow, inline: the compiler's own set, still real applications the compiler performs) and applied_callable_candidate (the qualified tokio::main path) — the nim shape one better: nim ruled the directive class away, this publishes it so a reader can discount it. The edge exists ONLY when the attribute arrives as a real attribute_item node whose next named sibling is the declaration; recovery text emits nothing and this fails. AND THE INNER-ATTRIBUTE REFUSAL IS PINNED (the rust lane's D1): `#![allow(unused)]` at the file head decorates the MODULE and has no declaration sibling, so it emits ZERO decorates rows and is COUNTED in metadata.unattributedEdges as `decorates:inner_attribute` — a class the analyzer previously did not count at all (202 inner sites over the whole population). The expectMetadata pin fails if the refusal goes silent again.
